minutes.headline: Water commissioners tabled the Bird Street district-expansion special-meeting request pending counsel's review; a lead-line grant was announced.
minutes.summary: The commissioners learned the district was approved for a DEP lead-line grant, discussed a PFAS public-education proposal to seek town ARPA funds, and heard a resident object to the pace of the H2 Properties special-meeting request for Bird Street. They tabled that request until the attorney weighs in, and also reviewed a camera/recording policy, a well number two pump test, and a Mass DOT permit for a main replacement. Minutes of April 12 and the chair position were handled by motion, and counsel was reappointed.

public_comment.topic: Said the H2 Properties letter asked for a public hearing rather than a special meeting, and urged a town-wide informational meeting with the town manager involved, with a longer notice period.
A resident (Miss Duffy) asked why the district must wait for counsel before arranging public information with the town.
A resident said the applicant LLC appears inactive and was reportedly ordered dissolved by a court in December; board asked her to forward the information.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of March 22 (one member abstained, having been absent)
Keep the current member as chairman (reorganization)
Reappoint counsel (complement and Paige) for the next year

budget_items.what_was_said: District received the DEP letter approving a lead service line grant; it replaces what would have been a paid requirement and funds equipment for GIS mapping.
Proposals for PFAS public education, master plan and pilot study to be submitted for town ARPA funds; town has received many applications and funds must be allocated in 2023 and spent by about 2025.
Residents find test prices varying from free to several hundred dollars.
District expects possible class action money; an earlier MTBE settlement brought in a few hundred thousand.

decisions.decision: Table the H2 Properties special-meeting request until the next meeting pending the attorney's review and timeline.
Superintendent/manager will send the PFAS education proposal to the town (Heather) and present to the selectmen.
Send the camera/recording policy to the attorney/counsel to start review, with an edit that individual recordings be announced prior to starting.
Commissioners will present at the selectmen's meeting next Tuesday, not as a posted district meeting.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners tabled the H2 Properties special-meeting request for Bird Street until the next meeting, pending the attorney's review and timeline.
Commissioners voted by voice to reappoint counsel for the next year.
The district reported a DEP letter approving a lead service line grant, which also funds equipment for GIS mapping.
The PFAS public-education proposal will go to the town to seek ARPA funds, then to the selectmen.
The camera and recording policy goes to counsel for review, with an edit that individual recordings be announced before they start.

why_it_matters: The Bird Street request could lead to a district-wide special meeting vote, and it is now waiting on counsel, so residents have more time to weigh in before any meeting is posted.
The lead-line grant and the PFAS education request for town ARPA funds touch water quality work and water-district costs, and ARPA money must be allocated in 2023, so the timing is tight.
